ety.text: Representing yeah pronounced with the mouth snapped closed at the end (excrescent /p/): yeah + -p.

ex: But you positively must have much, much more than the laconic "yups" and "nups" of the John Waynes and Gary Coopers...
She'd ask him a question that couldn't be answered by a "yup" or a "nope.

fr:ouais.gl: synonym of oui; yeah, yep, yup, yes, affirmative expression

ety.text: From oui via dialectal variants; also possibly from oyez.
Inherited from Latin iam (“already, now”). Cognate with Portuguese já and Spanish ya.
Possibly a calque of English yep.

Proto-Indo-European *sóder. Proto-Italic *sei Latin sī Proto-Indo-European *ḱe Proto-Italic *ke Latin -ce Latin sīce Latin sīc Old Galician-Portuguese si Portuguese nãoinflu. Portuguese miminflu. Portuguese sim Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese si (“yes”), influenced by não or mim.
